item.title: Meet Ime Udoka, Nigerian-American coach leading Houston Rockets in the NBA
item.description: Nigerian-American basketball coach Ime Udoka has built an impressive career in basketball, rising from representing Nigeria on the international stage to coaching some of the biggest teams in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Udoka, who currently serves as head coach of the Houston Rockets, has established himself as one of the prominent coaching figures in American basketball, with a career shaped by years of playing, coaching and leadership experience. Born on August 9, 1977, in Portland, Oregon, United States, Udoka has Nigerian roots and represented Nigeria in international basketball competitions before transitioning into coaching. His playing career included spells in the NBA, the NBA Development League and professional basketball leagues in Europe. He also played for Nigeria at the 2005 and 2011 FIBA AfroBasket tournaments, helping raise the country’s profile in international basketball. After retiring from professional basketball, Udoka moved into coaching, beginning his NBA coaching career as an assistant with the San Antonio Spurs in 2012. He worked under legendary coach Gregg Popovich, gaining experience in player development, team management and tactical preparation. During his time with San Antonio, the Spurs reached the NBA Finals in 2013 and won the championship in 2014, providing Udoka with valuable experience at the highest level of the sport. He subsequently served as an assistant coach with the Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets before joining the Boston Celtics in 2021. Led Boston Celtics to NBA Finals Udoka’s breakthrough as a head coach came in 2021 when he was appointed to lead the Boston Celtics. In his first season, he guided the team to the 2022 NBA Finals, where they faced the Golden State Warriors. Although Boston lost the series 4-2, Udoka earned recognition for transforming the team’s defensive performance and guiding its players through a successful playoff campaign. His achievement made him one of the few coaches to reach the NBA Finals in his first season as a head coach. However, his tenure in Boston ended in September 2022 when the franchise suspended him for the 2022–23 season over violations of team policies. New chapter with Houston Rockets In April 2023, the Houston Rockets appointed Udoka as their head coach, giving him another opportunity to lead an NBA franchise. He took charge of a rebuilding team that had struggled in previous seasons and was tasked with improving its competitiveness through tactical discipline, player development and stronger defensive organisation. His appointment marked another significant milestone in his coaching career, as he became responsible for developing a young Houston squad and guiding the franchise towards sustained success. Udoka’s coaching approach has been associated with defensive intensity, accountability and high expectations for players. item.title: Nigeria’s future depends on mentally resilient youths — Mamora
item.description: Former minister urges graduates to embrace purpose, adaptability, continuous learning By Adeola Badru Former Minister of Health, Olorunnimbe Mamora, has said Nigeria’s future depends largely on the mental resilience, character development and sense of purpose of its youths, warning that academic qualifications alone are insufficient to prepare them for the challenges of the modern world. Mamora said young Nigerians must develop the capacity to navigate economic uncertainties, technological disruptions and changing employment opportunities through adaptability, continuous learning and problem-solving skills. He spoke while delivering the 18th Convocation Lecture of Ajayi Crowther University (ACU), Oyo, titled, “Youths’ Mental Health and Purpose: Thriving in a Volatile World.” The former minister challenged graduating students to look beyond the certificates they had earned and prepare for a world where success would increasingly depend on their ability to manage uncertainty, identify opportunities and remain relevant. He described convocation as a transition into a new phase of life, requiring graduates to demonstrate resilience, discipline, adaptability and a clear sense of purpose. Mamora identified the growing influence of social media, economic pressures and rapid technological advancement as emerging challenges to the mental wellbeing of young people. While acknowledging that the internet had expanded access to information and opportunities, he noted that excessive engagement with digital platforms could contribute to loneliness, anxiety and unhealthy comparisons. He urged graduates not to measure their achievements or personal worth against the lifestyles and apparent successes of others on social media. “Do not allow social media platforms to become the mirror through which you measure your worth. “Your value is not determined by the number of people who like your photograph. Stop comparing your backstage with somebody else’s stage,” he said. On the changing employment landscape, particularly with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Mamora said graduates must recognise that education should go beyond acquiring academic qualifications. He stressed the importance of critical thinking, problem-solving, skills acquisition and continuous learning, noting that adaptability would be essential to remaining relevant in the evolving world of work. Drawing inspiration from the life of Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther, after whom the university was named, Mamora said the cleric’s journey from slavery to becoming a renowned missionary and scholar demonstrated the importance of determination and resilience in overcoming adversity. He urged the graduates to draw inspiration from Crowther’s life and remain committed to their aspirations despite the challenges they might encounter. item.title: Omo-Agege denies snubbing police invitation over Uduere killings
item.description: Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has denied reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. In a statement on Friday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the former Deputy President of the Senate said he had seen the reports and described them as untrue. “Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has seen the reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. “It isn’t true. You can’t turn down an invitation you never received,” he said. According to the statement, no formal invitation has reached the Senator or his office. “No letter has reached the Senator or his office, and no officer has come to him with one. He first learned of it the same way everyone else did, from the Command’s announcement in the media.” Areh said the report that Omo-Agege refused to appear was based on a single unnamed source. “The claim that he refused leans on a single unnamed source. The Senator hasn’t told the police, or anyone else, that he won’t appear.” The statement also revisited the events at Uduere, insisting that Omo-Agege was the victim of the attack. “It is worth remembering what happened at Uduere. Senator Omo-Agege was the target of an assassination attempt. Senior members of his campaign team were murdered, and others are still in hospital with serious injuries. “He is the one who survived an attack on his life, and the one demanding that those responsible be found and prosecuted.” Omo-Agege said he wants the case resolved and justice for the victims. “He wants this case resolved, and he wants justice for the dead and the wounded. If the police serve a lawful invitation, he will honour it. He asks only that it be sent through his office so a date can be agreed.” He faulted the manner in which the alleged invitation was made public. “A summons announced in the press before it reaches the person named is not due process, and he won’t be tried in the media,” he said. item.title: 2027: National Counter Terrorism Centre moves to foil attacks on INEC facilities, personnel
item.description: ..Laka warns against electoral violence, voter intimidation, destruction of infrastructure By Kingsley Omonobi The National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), Office of the National Security Adviser, has said it is working with security agencies to prevent planned attacks on Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) offices, personnel and electoral infrastructure ahead of the 2027 general elections. The National Coordinator of the Centre, Major General Adamu Laka, also said measures were being strengthened to protect voters and prevent emerging security threats from disrupting the electoral process. Laka spoke at the National Flag-off/North Central Zone Town Hall Engagement on Preventing Electoral Violence and Strengthening Election Security in Nigeria. He urged youths not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, describing them as critical stakeholders in the country’s democratic future. “In this regard, I urge our young people not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence. You are important stakeholders in Nigeria’s democratic future and your energy, creativity and influence should be directed towards promoting peace, tolerance and responsible civic participation,” he said. He said the Centre was working towards preventing attacks on INEC offices and personnel, protecting voters and electoral infrastructure, countering fake news and inflammatory narratives, strengthening community-based early warning systems and ensuring timely responses to emerging security threats. Describing elections as the heartbeat of democracy, Laka said their credibility depended not only on the conduct of voting and announcement of results but also on the peace, security and public confidence surrounding the entire electoral process. “There is absolutely no gain in any loss of life or property as a result of this democratic process,” he said. The NCTC coordinator identified misinformation and disinformation, hate speech, political intolerance, incitement, youth manipulation, political thuggery, vote buying, voter intimidation, voter suppression and destruction of public infrastructure as factors that could fuel electoral violence. He said stakeholders must collectively address the threats and strengthen early warning and response mechanisms to identify potential dangers before they escalate into violence. Laka also stressed the need to build public confidence in the electoral process and ensure that women, youths, persons with disabilities and internally displaced persons were not excluded from meaningful participation. He maintained that preventing electoral violence was not the responsibility of security agencies alone but required the collective commitment of political actors, government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the media and community-based organisations. item.title: ADC waste plan will create 21,000 jobs in Lagos – Gbadamosi
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) deputy governorship candidate Babatunde Olalere Gbadamosi has projected that the party’s waste management plan would create at least 21,000 jobs in Lagos, including 20,000 for waste collection crews. Gbadamosi, who is running with ADC governorship candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, spoke at the Road to Election 2027 Lagos Deputy Governorship Debate on Nigeria Info FM on Friday, where he outlined proposals on employment, waste collection, housing and transportation. Addressing unemployment, Gbadamosi said he did not know the state’s unemployment rate and disputed figures published by the Lagos government. He proposed a review of public sector salaries and said his plans for waste management, housing, transportation and education would create jobs for Lagosians. “First of all, the truth is, I suppose the truth is, I really don’t know what the unemployment rate is. Whatever figures that are put out by the APC government of Lagos State are usually just false. They just manufacture figures, yank them out of their a**,” he said. He said he and Rhodes-Vivour had agreed to “undertake a review, a wholesale review of public sector salaries, in order to bring them in line with our current economic realities.” He also cited plans for 20,000 jobs in waste-to-energy, 100,000 affordable housing units and 16,000 electric buses. “We plan to bring 16,000 electric buses into Lagos State because we simply don’t have enough capacity to carry the 24 million people of Lagos State on the current transportation system,” he said, adding that the housing and transport plans would also provide work for young people. On waste collection, Gbadamosi proposed providing each local government with at least 200 dumpsters. He estimated that 4,000 trucks, each with a five-person crew, would create 20,000 jobs. “All right, we have 20 local governments. So 200 times 20, that’s 4000 trucks. 4000 trucks times five crew members, each. That’s already 20,000 jobs,” he said. He estimated that recycling centres would create at least another 1,000 jobs, based on a minimum of 50 workers at each of 20 local government centres. “That’s 50 jobs times 20 local governments. That’s already what 1000 extra jobs minimum,” he said, adding that the programme would be funded with “25% of Lagos State revenue that is being paid to Alpha Beta at the moment.” Other major contenders at the debate included Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) deputy governorship candidate Moriam Tolani Animashaun and Social Democratic Party (SDP) deputy candidate Kayode Evelyn Aderiyike. item.title: PANDEF rejects 20% NCDMB fund deduction for research council
item.description: …Warns against diversion of local content funds, urges NASS to review proposed legislation By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has rejected the proposed 20 per cent deduction from the Nigerian Content Development Fund to finance the proposed National Council on Research, Science, Technology and Innovation. The forum warned that the move could undermine years of investment in indigenous industrial capacity and weaken the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), which has been instrumental in promoting local expertise, skills acquisition, enterprise development and industrialisation. PANDEF urged the National Assembly to review Section 19 of the proposed legislation establishing the council and reject the provision earmarking 20 per cent of the Nigerian Content Development Fund for its financing. Addressing journalists in Abuja on Friday, PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, acknowledged the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen the country’s research, science, technology and innovation capacity but expressed concern over Part IV, Section 19(a) of the proposed Bill. He described the proposed funding arrangement as inappropriate, counterproductive and fundamentally flawed, arguing that a new national institution should not be financed by weakening an existing statutory agency with clearly defined responsibilities and ongoing development commitments. Igali said the NCDMB, which commenced operations in 2010, had a statutory mandate to promote the development, acquisition and application of indigenous capacity in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry. He noted that the Nigerian Content Development Fund was already supporting strategic investments in the oil and gas sector and related areas, including agriculture, manufacturing and transportation. According to him, diverting 20 per cent of the fund could disrupt existing commitments, constrain ongoing investments and slow the progress recorded in local content development. “The Nigerian Content Development Fund is not an idle pool of resources awaiting allocation. It is an active development instrument that is already financing and supporting several strategic investments in the oil and gas industry and related sectors of the Nigerian economy,” he said. Igali also warned that the proposed funding mechanism could establish a dangerous precedent in public finance, whereby newly established government institutions would depend on deductions from funds already allocated to existing statutory agencies. item.title: Photos: Adeleke sworn in for 2nd term; says ‘Let’s heal our past wounds’
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As Governor Ademola Adeleke took oath of office for his second term tenure, he has charged the Osun State political class to allow the wounds of the past to heal and collaborate to develop the state. Governor Adeleke spoke while addressing hundreds of dignitaries and residents who thronged the Osogbo township stadium to be part of his inauguration. He disclosed that citizens, irrespective of political affiliations, must unite for the collective good. His words: “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content”. The governor commended the resilience of the citizens and residents of the state to safeguard democracy, saying their commitment has become a national model. “Today is a triumph of the people’s will. I give all glory to God and deeply thank the people of Osun. Their commitment to democracy is today a national model,” he said. 2nd term focus On his administration’s focus for the second term, he said the target of the government will focus on citizens’ welfare, infrastructure expansion, industrialisation, agricultural transformation, digital economy, tourism industry, wealth creation, and youth and women’s development among others. “As growth depends on steady power supply, we will immediately set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission. This is in line with the power sector law I signed earlier this year. “Job and Wealth creation will be at the heart of our second term. We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” Osun local government crisis On the issue of local government crisis, Adeleke said: “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter. In the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres.” Earlier, the deputy governor, Kola Adewusi took oath of office at 11:24a.m. followed by that of the governor whose oath of office was administered by the Chief Judge, Justice Oyebola Adepele-Ojo at exactly 11:34am. Vice President Shettima, Ooni, others Meanwhile, the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima led dignitaries from all spheres of life to the inauguration. The National leader of the APC, Chief Bisi Akande; Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa; former National Secretary of the party, Senator Iyiola Omisore, PDP’s National Treasurer, Prince Diran Odeyemi and former Presidential candidate of the Labour Party, Datti-Baba Ahmed, were also in attendance. item.title: [PHOTOS] Adeleke Sworn In For Second Term As Osun Governor
item.description: Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has been sworn in for a second term, beginning another four-year tenure that will run until 2030. Adeleke took the oath of office on Friday, November 27, 2026, at an inauguration ceremony held at the Osogbo Township Stadium. The state Chief Judge administered the oath of office to Deputy Governor Kola Adewusi before swearing in Adeleke. The ceremony was attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima, who led several dignitaries, including former Osun State Governor Bisi Akande, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa, and former Senate President Bukola Saraki. The entertainment industry was also represented, with Afrobeats singer Davido, alongside B-Red and Shina Rambo, attending the ceremony to celebrate the governor. Adeleke secured re-election in the August 15, 2026 governorship election on the platform of the Accord Party after defecting from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). He polled 511,067 votes to defeat the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, who secured 444,815 votes. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term. item.title: Full list: African countries where travelers can access without visa
item.description: Travelling across Africa is becoming easier as more countries adopt visa-free entry policies aimed at promoting tourism, strengthening regional integration and encouraging trade among African nations. Several African countries have introduced policies allowing citizens of other African countries to visit without obtaining a visa before travelling, reducing the cost and administrative hurdles associated with cross-border movement. Among the countries offering such access are Benin, The Gambia, Rwanda, Seychelles, Ghana and Togo. The policies form part of wider efforts to improve freedom of movement across the continent and advance the African Union’s goal of greater economic integration. The six countries are highlighted below, although their entry arrangements are not identical. 1. Benin Benin is one of Africa’s leading supporters of visa-free movement. It allows citizens of other African countries to enter without obtaining a visa before travelling. The country has promoted easier cross-border movement to encourage tourism, business and regional cooperation. 2. The Gambia The Gambia offers visa-free entry to citizens of other African countries. It is one of the continent’s more open destinations, making it attractive to visitors interested in tourism, business and cultural exchanges. 3. Rwanda Rwanda allows citizens of African Union member states to enter without a visa. The policy supports the country’s efforts to attract African visitors, investors and business travellers. 4. Seychelles Seychelles operates a visa-free entry policy for visitors of all nationalities, including African travellers. However, visitors must obtain the required travel authorisation before departure and meet the country’s entry conditions. 5. Ghana Ghana introduced a free visa policy for African nationals in May 2026. Under the arrangement, African travellers can apply for electronic visas without paying visa fees. However, an application and approval are still required, meaning the policy is not strictly visa-free entry. 6. Togo Togo has introduced visa-free entry for African passport holders, subject to pre-arrival requirements. The policy is part of efforts to facilitate movement across the continent and strengthen regional integration. item.title: Kano govt to Kwankwaso: Stop dragging Yusuf into EFCC troubles
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government has asked former Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso to stop linking Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf to his alleged dealings with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). The government said Yusuf had no involvement in Kwankwaso’s issues with the anti-graft agency, which it claimed predated the current administration. The Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, stated this in a statement issued on Friday. He described Kwankwaso’s allegations against the governor as misleading and politically motivated. According to the government, it was wrong for the former governor to accuse Yusuf of influencing the EFCC investigation when the matter began before his administration. “The crisis and court cases involving the NDC are internal party matters arising from disagreements among its members, and the Kano State Government has no involvement in them,” the statement said. The government accused Kwankwaso of using the governor as a target to gain public sympathy and remain politically relevant ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Rather than constantly blaming the Kano State Government for his political difficulties, Kwankwaso should concentrate on resolving the internal challenges confronting his political camp,” the statement said. It maintained that Yusuf was elected to govern Kano State and deliver development, not to engage in political arguments or take responsibility for the problems of other political parties. The government urged Kwankwaso to allow the administration to focus on fulfilling its promises to the people, warning that attempts to gain public sympathy through political blackmail would not succeed. “You cannot win public sympathy through blackmail and unfounded allegations,” it said. The statement added that the people of Kano State would have the opportunity to judge political leaders through their votes in 2027. It further reaffirmed that Yusuf remained committed to governance, development and the welfare of residents. Recall that Kwankwaso had accused Governor Yusuf of using the EFCC and other government institutions to target him and members of his family for political reasons ahead of the 2027 elections. He also alleged that the governor attempted to pressure the EFCC through protests at its office and interfere in a case involving the NDC governorship candidate. item.title: Obasanjo unhappy Tinubu is delivering on promises — FHA director
item.description: B y Dapo Akinrefon An Executive Director (Projects Implementation) of the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Oluremi Omowaiye, has criticised former President Olusegun Obasanjo over his remarks on President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, alleging that the former president was uncomfortable with the achievements of the current administration. Omowaiye, who defended Tinubu’s economic policies, said Obasanjo was unhappy because the President had achieved what he failed to accomplish during his eight years in office. Obasanjo had criticised the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, arguing that they had pushed many Nigerians deeper into poverty. However, reacting to the former president’s position in a statement on Friday, Omowaiye, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), said Obasanjo should be ashamed of his comments, insisting that Tinubu had surpassed his achievements. “Obasanjo should cover his face in shame. He is unhappy because we have Yoruba man who has done what he failed to do as president. He is uncomfortable because President Tinubu has surpassed his achievements,” he said. The FHA director further alleged that Obasanjo was uncomfortable with Tinubu’s performance because the President was delivering on his promises and could secure another four-year term in 2027. “Obasanjo is unhappy because President Tinubu is delivering on his promises and he knows he is going to achieve much more when he gets reelected for another four years. That is why he is doing everything to stop it but he won’t succeed. “Nigerians are happy with the President’s Renewed Hope agenda and they want him to continue,” Omowaiye said. Questioning Obasanjo’s claim that Tinubu’s reforms had made Nigerians 300 per cent poorer, Omowaiye argued that the former president’s business interests continued to operate despite the economic difficulties he had highlighted. He specifically cited Bells University and Obasanjo Farms, asking whether the former president had shut down either business because of the financial challenges facing Nigerians. “Did he close down Bells University because students are unable to pay? No. Has he closed down Obasanjo Farms because the economy is so bad?” he asked. Omowaiye also cited Next Cash and Carry supermarket, which he described as Nigeria’s biggest single supermarket, arguing that its continued operation after a fire incident demonstrated that businesses could still thrive despite economic challenges. “Peter Obi that Obasanjo is supporting has the biggest single supermarket in Nigeria. It got burnt sometimes ago. He rebuilt it and it is doing fine today. If the economy is so bad, will Next Supermarket be doing fine?” he queried. He also faulted Obasanjo over the state of infrastructure during his presidency, particularly the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, which he described as the country’s most economically viable road. item.description: Manchester United are error-prone, leaky at the back, and desperately short of confidence as they face the growing nightmare of a Premier League relegation battle. Talk of the Red Devils going down still appears fanciful, but analysts at Opta say they have a 27 percent chance of dropping into the Championship as they prepare to host impressive Brentford. At the top end of the table, Manchester City’s match at Arsenal appears to be a must-win for Enzo Maresca’s team, who have fallen off the pace after a barren spell. AFP Sport looks at three talking points ahead of the weekend action: United’s error count Midfielder Kobbie Mainoo warned “no one’s coming to save us” after Manchester United’s 4-0 hammering by Liverpool last week left them in the relegation zone. Manchester United’s Dutch forward #11 Joshua Zirkzee (C) and teammates react to their defeat on the pitch after the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United on November 22, 2026. (Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP) More mistakes, notably from goalkeeper Senne Lammens — together with some controversial refereeing decisions — cost them a morale-boosting Champions League win at Sporting Lisbon in midweek. Following their 2-2 draw, United had conceded the most goals (36), the most penalties (five), and had received the most red cards (five) of any Premier League team this season across all competitions. New manager Mauricio Pochettino will now be in no doubt as to the scale of the job at Old Trafford as United chase just their second league win of the season against Brentford. “I think we need to encourage and we need to really believe in our play,” Pochettino told TNT Sports after Wednesday’s match in Portugal. “We need to believe more and more and more.” But until he finds a way to cut out individual errors, opponents will always fancy their chances against the struggling giants. Blunt Arsenal Manchester United’s Danish defender #13 Patrick Dorgu (R) vies with Liverpool’s Uruguayan defender #33 Ronald Araujo (L) during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Paul ELLIS / AFP) Champions Arsenal, despite their impressive results, are showing a worrying inability to kill off opponents. In their past nine matches in all competitions, the Gunners have won just one game by more than a single goal. They had 30 shots in their midweek 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund, but just four of those were on target. Kai Havertz has a paltry three Premier League goals this season while fellow forward Viktor Gyokeres has yet to get off the mark in the top flight. “The feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put (in) that kind of performance, the amount of chances, the situation,” Arteta said after the Dortmund draw. “There is an element of luck, there is an element of us finishing the actions better.” City, already six points behind Arsenal, travel to the Emirates low on confidence after t

item.title: Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim that boxer has schizophrenia
item.description: Paris Fury, the wife of British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury, has withdrawn her earlier claim that her husband was diagnosed with schizophrenia, clarifying that he has never been formally diagnosed with the condition. Paris made the clarification after an earlier version of an upcoming Netflix documentary about the boxer featured her describing him as having “mild schizophrenia”. In a statement, she said she had used the term while recalling a conversation about Tyson’s mental health struggles several years ago, but acknowledged that it was not an accurate description of his medical history. “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” she said. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” She added that mental health was complex and that finding the right words to describe someone’s experiences was not always easy. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love,” she said. Paris also praised her husband for speaking openly about his struggles and thanked the public for supporting their family. Netflix confirmed that it had updated the documentary following the family’s clarification about Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis. “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch,” the streaming platform said. The earlier comments had attracted attention from the British Boxing Board of Control, which indicated that it was investigating the matter. The 38 year old boxer is scheduled to face Joshua in an all British heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11, with the vacant WBA title expected to be at stake. Tyson has previously spoken publicly about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, when he became world heavyweight champion. After the victory, he took a break of nearly three years from boxing, during which he battled suicidal thoughts, drug and alcohol problems, and significant weight gain. Reflecting on that period in the documentary, Tyson said he experienced severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” he said. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.” He later returned to boxing and regained the world heavyweight title by defeating Deontay Wilder in February 2020. item.title: Arsenic In The Water: Thailand Presses Myanmar Over Mining Pollution
item.description: As pollution mounts in its rivers, food and water, Thailand is pressing neighbouring Myanmar to tackle unregulated mining, while urging China to exert its influence in the war-ravaged nation. Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits. Bangkok this week hosted the first Thai-Myanmar working group on the issue — also attended by the Chinese ambassador — where it said tests proved rare-earth and gold mines in Myanmar were causing the pollution downstream. The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. This photo taken on June 5, 2026 shows Wan Wiriya, assistant professor from Chiang Mai University, showing the results of an arsenic level test from a water sample (C) taken from the Kok River, next to a control sample of drinking water (R) near the the northern Thai city of Chiang Rai. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP But there was no public agreement to Thailand’s request for a six-month suspension of operations, and how one could be implemented remains unclear, with Myanmar’s military not in full control. Bangkok is also looking to China, the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, to pressure private Chinese operators, as a months-long concern becomes increasingly urgent. Authorities warned residents this week against eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests in northern and northeastern Thailand found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead. Saengwaree Suvirakan, a farmer from Tha Ton in Chiang Mai province who joined a protest in Bangkok this week, said fish stocks were declining in any case. “Now with the mines the fish are all gone,” she said. ‘Not from nature’ This photo taken on June 4, 2026 shows fishermen and their boats near the confluence of the Kok River and Mekong River in Chiang Saen, northern Thailand’s Chiang Rai province. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP At the joint talks, Thai ministers said high arsenic levels in the Kok and Sai rivers could only have come from rare-earth and gold mines on the Myanmar side. “Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar’s) Shan state, no-one disagrees,” Science Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said. But how to tackle it remains an issue. Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), welcomed the agreement on joint sampling sites. “This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity,” he told AFP. But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be “really difficult”, he added. Multiple ethnic armed groups have been operating there for decades, while a 2021 military coup sparked an ongoing civil war. item.title: Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas
item.description: Italy has listed 14 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for work visas under its 2026–2028 immigration programme, offering employment opportunities to foreign workers across several sectors of its economy. Nigeria is among the African countries on the list, alongside Ghana, Senegal, Morocco, Egypt and 10 others. The programme forms part of Italy’s broader labour migration policy, which seeks to admit foreign workers to address labour shortages and meet the country’s employment needs. Under the programme, the Italian government has reserved 25,000 work permits annually for citizens of 38 designated countries, including the 14 African nations. The African countries named are: Algeria Ivory Coast Egypt Ethiopia The Gambia Ghana Mali Morocco Mauritius Niger Nigeria Senegal Sudan Tunisia. The employment opportunities cover sectors including agriculture, forestry, fishing, food production, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, tourism, transportation, logistics, healthcare and social assistance. According to the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the immigration programme provides for a total of 497,550 foreign workers to enter Italy between 2026 and 2028. The allocation is divided into 164,850 workers for 2026, 165,850 for 2027 and 166,850 for 2028. The figures cover seasonal and non-seasonal employment as well as self-employment. However, inclusion on the list does not automatically guarantee a work visa. Applicants must secure employment from an Italian employer, who is generally required to apply for the relevant work authorisation, known as nulla osta , before the worker proceeds with the visa application. For the 2026 allocation, applications for seasonal agricultural jobs were scheduled to open on January 12, while those for seasonal tourism jobs were scheduled for February 9. Applications for non-seasonal employment under the relevant categories were scheduled for February 16 and 18, 2026. The programme is part of Italy’s efforts to address labour shortages through regulated migration while strengthening cooperation with countries of origin. item.title: UK Reform leader vows to scrap Graduate visa route used by 20,478 Nigerians
item.description: UK Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, has vowed to scrap the United Kingdom’s Graduate visa route if his party wins power, a move that could affect thousands of Nigerians who use the scheme to remain in the country after completing their studies. Farage announced the proposal in a post on X on Thursday, arguing that the route allows foreign graduates to stay in the UK for two years after completing their degrees, competing with British workers for entry level jobs or potentially claiming asylum. Figures published by the UK Home Office on November 26 showed that 20,478 Nigerian nationals received grants under the Graduate route in the year to September 2026, making Nigerians the third largest group of beneficiaries. Indian nationals topped the list with 66,552 grants, followed by Pakistanis with 24,768. The three nationalities accounted for about 69 per cent of all grants recorded during the period. The Graduate route allows international students who have completed eligible courses at UK universities to remain in the country and work or look for employment without needing an immediate job offer or sponsorship. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has described the scheme as “a scam on the British people” and proposed replacing it with a 30 day period for graduates to secure a qualifying job that meets an economic value test. The party said about 800,000 Graduate visas, including those issued to dependants, had been granted since the route was introduced in July 2021. Yusuf also cited Home Office figures showing that 5,130 asylum claims were made by people who had previously held Graduate visas in the year to June 2026, twice the number recorded in the preceding year. The pledge comes as the Labour government is already preparing to reduce the standard duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months from January 1, 2027. The change will not apply to graduates from institutions that meet certain compliance and labour market outcome standards. However, Reform UK has yet to clarify how its proposed abolition would affect people who already hold Graduate visas or international students currently studying in the country. The latest Home Office figures also showed a decline in the number of Nigerian students receiving sponsored study visas. Grants to Nigerian nationals fell by 34 per cent to 19,734 in the year to September 2026, representing about six per cent of the total. item.title: UN warns of worsening hunger in northern Nigeria, 15 other areas
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The United Nations has warned of worsening hunger across 16 regions of the world over the next six months, identifying northern Nigeria, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia and Yemen as areas facing the highest risk of acute food insecurity. The warning was contained in a joint report by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP), which attributed the growing food crisis to armed conflicts, climate extremes, economic shocks and declining humanitarian assistance. The report, released on Friday, covers the period from December 2026 to May 2027 and cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further in several African countries as conflict and extreme weather events continue to disrupt livelihoods and food production. It identified Sudan and South Sudan as countries where famine remains a plausible risk, particularly in parts of North Darfur. The agencies also expressed concern over rising political violence, noting that incidents had increased by more than 15 per cent compared with the same period last year. The development, according to the report, has triggered significant displacement in recent months, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen, further worsening the humanitarian situation. It also highlighted a sharp decline in humanitarian funding to the five countries facing the highest levels of concern. According to the agencies, humanitarian assistance to the countries fell by nearly two-thirds between 2022 and 2025, dropping from $5.1bn to $2bn. “While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” the report stated. The agencies warned that previous humanitarian interventions had helped prevent famine in affected areas, but the improvements were often temporary, with severe food insecurity returning within a few years. Other areas classified as facing very high concern include Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Palestine and Haiti. The report noted that gang violence in Haiti had displaced about 1.5 million people and disrupted humanitarian access, while the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to grapple with an Ebola outbreak. Chad, Uganda, Southern Africa and the Central American Dry Corridor were also added to the list of hunger hotspots. The agencies warned that the impact of El Niño could worsen food production in several of these regions, particularly through irregular rainfall, drought and flooding.
